Use NPL(null) = −1. During a leftist-heap merge, the recursive call has returned. At the current root, the left child’s NPL is 1 and the right child’s NPL is 3. After restoring the leftist property, the root’s NPL becomes 4.

Let L and R be non-empty splay trees with distinct keys, and suppose every key in L is smaller than every key in R. After splaying the maximum key of L to its root, attaching R as that root’s right subtree produces a valid binary search tree without any further rotations.

Consider $F(0)=0$, $F(1)=1$, and $F(k)=F(k-1)+F(k-2)$ for $k\geq 2$. A top-down implementation memoizes every computed value, including the base cases, and performs constant-time table lookups. Even with this memoization, evaluating $F(n)$ requires exponentially many function calls because each uncached non-base call makes two recursive calls. Treat arithmetic as unit cost.

A B+ tree has a root with separator 21 and two leaves [3, 9, 14] and [21, 26]. Each leaf holds at most three data keys; an overflowing four-key leaf splits into two leaves of two keys each. Internal nodes hold at most three child pointers, and each separator is the minimum key of its right child subtree. After inserting 12, the key 12 appears both in the root and in a leaf, while the tree height is unchanged.

Define the height of an empty tree as −1 and that of a leaf as 0. Among all AVL trees of height 4, a tree with the minimum number of nodes must have root subtrees containing 7 and 4 nodes, in either order.

A standard binomial queue contains at most one binomial tree of each order. If its roots are stored in a linked list, and there is no cached minimum pointer. If the queue contains exactly $2^k$ elements, where $k\geq 1$, finding the minimum by scanning its root list takes $\Theta(1)$ time.
By the master theorem, the solution to the recurrence $T(n)=4T(n/4)+\log n$ is $O(n\log n)$.

The 0-1 Knapsack problem is defined as: Given a knapsack with a maximum weight capacity W, and n items. Each item i has a weight $w_i>0$ and a profit $p_i>0$. We can either select the whole item or discard it (cannot take a fraction of an item). The goal is to choose a subset of items such that the sum of their weights does not exceed W, while the total profit is maximized.

The function Knapsack01 is to solve the 0-1 Knapsack problem by backtracking. W is the capacity of the knapsack; n objects are stored in array s; array x stores a feasible solution; val is the current total profit; r is the current total profit of the remaining sub-problem; i is the index of the object s[i] to be checked; the optimal solution is stored in optx and the optimal profit in optp. The values are initialized as shown. Please complete the program.
